content.value: Compare algorithms by counting operations as the input grows. A traversal has work proportional to the number of elements. Independent nested loops multiply their counts; sequential loops add them. A loop whose range is halved repeatedly grows much more slowly than a full traversal. Describe best and worst cases instead of assuming every input takes the same work.
For n = 4, the inner loop runs 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 times. Doubling a large n approximately quadruples this work. Count loop-body executions rather than elapsed seconds, which depend on hardware.
Practice: trace the example by hand, change one input, and explain how the result changes. Check an empty or boundary case when the preconditions allow it.
